messages:
sanjay: Heads-up — nightly eval zh_formality suite jumped from 3 failures to 47. Many outputs switch to English and/or append emojis (e.g. 😊).
sanjay: Example failure (prompt and model output):
```
Prompt: 请把下面这封邮件改得更正式:
亲爱的张伟，周一开会见。谢谢。
Model output: Sure, here's a more professional version: Dear Zhang Wei, Let's meet on Monday. Thanks! 😊
```
hao: who ran the nightly and which model/quantization variant? :thinking:
ellie: nightlies used `rwd-3b-int8-2026-03-18` by default this week.
marie: can you reproduce locally? command to run: `python eval/run_eval.py --suite zh_formality --model rwd-3b-int8-2026-03-18 --seed 42 --max-tokens 256`
sanjay: ran locally — reproduced: 52/120 bad outputs with EN fallback/emoji. Quick postproc (strip emoji) drops fails to 12, so not all are emoji-only.
eval-bot: nightly job 1738450000 finished. results: gs://redwood-evals/nightly/1738456789/results.json
hao: hypothesis: quant mapping introduced token id shifts so some rare punctuation/emoji codepoints get emitted for certain tokenization paths. check vocab remap around IDs used for punctuation and emojis.
ellie: can we bisect on quant rollout? try fp16 baseline vs int8 older vs int8 current.
sanjay: tested: `rwd-3b-fp16-2026-03-10` -> no emoji, `rwd-3b-int8-2026-03-15` -> no emoji, `rwd-3b-int8-2026-03-18` -> emoji surge. looks like change in 03-18 quant step.
marie: good bisection. likely runtime/quant kernel change. open runtime/quant issue and tag eng-runtime.
hao: to debug, dump token ids for a failing output. example command: `python tools/token_debug.py --model rwd-3b-int8-2026-03-18 --text "Dear Zhang Wei, Let's meet on Monday. Thanks! 😊" --show-ids`
sanjay: token dump shows sequences where a punctuation token id (was 3012) becomes 128312 after quant remap and corresponds to emoji in unicode table used by tokenizer fallback. attaching snippet:
```
tokens: [102, 3452, 128312, 77, ...]
id->glyph: 128312 -> U+1F60A (😊)
```
ellie: that mapping is the smoking gun. looks like quant remap table got shifted or a fallback table got applied. :bug:
marie: mitigation: add a temporary postprocessing blacklist for any non-CJK unicode in zh_formality suite and add an eval assertion to fail the night if non-CJK characters appear. Also add a canary that runs `rwd-3b-fp16` to detect regressions earlier.
hao: I'll dig into the quant kernel commit on 03-18 and confirm whether remap table or tokenizer fallback was modified. assigning to @hao in GH.
sanjay: filed GH issue #2345: "int8-2026-03-18 quant remap causes non-CJK emoji outputs in zh_formality" with reproduction, token dumps, and links to nightly results. /cc @eng-runtime @eng-ml
marie: thanks. can we also add a short-term rule in the inference runtime to avoid emitting emoji codepoints when serving zh locales? just as a guardrail until runtime fix.
hao: yes I can prototype a runtime guard (locale-based emoji suppression) but prefer to fix the remap root cause. will PR both: immediate guard + root cause patch.
sanjay: added the eval assertion and temporary postproc in the nightly pipeline. will remove after runtime fix verified. thanks all :thumbsup:
ellie: great triage. next steps: (1) runtime investigation @hao, (2) nightly assertion stays on, (3) revert postproc after fix.
marie: updating incident board + escalate to eng-runtime on-call.
eval-bot: nightly alert created: alerts/zh_formality_non_cjk_tokens/1738456789
sanjay: keeping this thread updated with any new reproductions or logs.
